added_lemmas.statement: For every pair \((A,B)\) of normalized \(2\times2\) probability tables for which \(F(A,B)\neq\varnothing\), and every \((c,d)\in F(A,B)\), the handle \(Hthr\) constructs a finite model \(M\in MC(A,B)\) with binary, \(D\)-valued roots \(U0,V0\), a private root \(W0\) having at most eight support points, mutually independent roots, and one deterministic outcome function \(fY\) shared by all regimes, such that \(q=a+b-c+d\).  The construction reproduces all four cells of \(A\) and all four cells of \(B\), including on every support face where one or more natural-treatment strata have probability zero.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix normalized \(2\times2\) probability tables \(A,B\) and \((c,d)\in F(A,B)\).  Normalization and nonnegativity of the cells give
\[
0\le a\le p\le1,\qquad 0\le b\le r\le1,
\]
and
\[
0\le A(1,1)\le1-p,
\qquad
0\le B(1,1)\le1-r.
\]
All four stratum masses \(w00,w01,w10,w11\) are therefore nonnegative, and
\[
w00+w01+w10+w11
=pr+p(1-r)+(1-p)r+(1-p)(1-r)=1.
\]

Define the four desired success numerators
\[
n_{00}:=c,qquad n_{01}:=a-c,qquad
n_{10}:=b-c,qquad n_{11}:=d.
\]
By \(\text{def:mass-fiber}\),
\[
cL\le c\le cU,qquad 0\le d\le w11.
\]
Using the definitions of \(cL\) and \(cU\), these inequalities imply, equation by equation,
\[
0\le c\le w00,
\]
\[
c\le a\quad\text{and}\quad c\ge a-w01
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 0\le a-c\le w01,
\]
and
\[
c\le b\quad\text{and}\quad c\ge b-w10
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 0\le b-c\le w10.
\]
Together with the bound on \(d\), this proves
\[
0\le n_{ij}\le w_{ij}\qquad((i,j)\in D^2),
\]
where \(w_{00}=w00\), \(w_{01}=w01\), \(w_{10}=w10\), and \(w_{11}=w11\).

For each \((i,j)\in D^2\), define
\[
t_{ij}:=
\begin{cases}
n_{ij}/w_{ij},&w_{ij}>0,\\
0,&w_{ij}=0.
\end{cases}
\]
If \(w_{ij}>0\), the preceding bounds give \(0\le t_{ij}\le1\) and \(w_{ij}t_{ij}=n_{ij}\).  If \(w_{ij}=0\), those same bounds force \(n_{ij}=0\); hence the arbitrary null-stratum choice \(t_{ij}=0\) again gives \(0\le t_{ij}\le1\) and
\[
w_{ij}t_{ij}=n_{ij}.
\]
Thus this identity holds for all four strata without division by zero.

Define the two off-target response probabilities by
\[
\gamma_A:=
\begin{cases}
A(1,1)/(1-p),&1-p>0,\\
0,&1-p=0,
\end{cases}
\qquad
\gamma_B:=
\begin{cases}
B(1,1)/(1-r),&1-r>0,\\
0,&1-r=0.
\end{cases}
\]
If \(1-p=0\), nonnegativity and \(A(1,1)\le1-p\) force \(A(1,1)=0\); the analogous statement holds for \(B\) when \(1-r=0\).  Consequently, in all cases,
\[
0\le\gamma_A,\gamma_B\le1,
\qquad
(1-p)\gamma_A=A(1,1),
\qquad
(1-r)\gamma_B=B(1,1).
\]

On the product probability space, let \(U0,V0\) be independent \(D\)-valued roots with
\[
\mathbb P(U0=0)=p,qquad \mathbb P(V0=0)=r,
\]
and set \(fX(u)=u\) and \(fZ(v)=v\).  Degenerate choices \(p\in\{0,1\}\) or \(r\in\{0,1\}\) are allowed.  For \((x,z,u,v)\in D^4\), prescribe
\[
h(x,z,u,v):=
\begin{cases}
t_{uv},&(x,z)=(0,0),\\
\gamma_A,&(x,z)=(1,0),\\
\gamma_B,&(x,z)=(0,1),\\
1/2,&(x,z)=(1,1).
\end{cases}
\]
The set
\[
\mathcal H:=\{t_{00},t_{01},t_{10},t_{11},\gamma_A,\gamma_B,1/2\}
\]
has at most seven elements, all in \([0,1]\).  List the distinct elements of \(\mathcal H\cup\{0,1\}\) as
\[
0=\lambda_0<\lambda_1<\cdots<\lambda_m=1.
\]
There are at most nine listed values, so \(1\le m\le8\).  Let \(W0\), independent of \((U0,V0)\), take values in \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\) with
\[
\mathbb P(W0=k)=\lambda_k-\lambda_{k-1},
\qquad 1\le k\le m.
\]
The masses are strictly positive and telescope to one.  Put
\[
g(e,k):=\mathbf 1\{\lambda_k\le e\}.
\]
For every \(e=\lambda_j\in\mathcal H\), including \(e=0\) and \(e=1\),
\[
\mathbb P\{g(e,W0)=1\}
=\sum_{k=1}^{j}(\lambda_k-\lambda_{k-1})
=\lambda_j=e.
\]
Define the single deterministic outcome assignment
\[
fY(x,z,u,v,k):=g(h(x,z,u,v),k).
\]
This is one function on all arguments and is therefore shared by every intervention.  The product construction makes \(U0,V0,W0\) mutually independent, and \(W0\) has at most eight support points.

We now check all eight reported cells.  Under \(\operatorname{do}(Z=0)\), the threshold identity and source independence give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P_M(X=0,Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=0))
&=w00t_{00}+w01t_{01}\\
&=n_{00}+n_{01}=c+(a-c)=a=A(0,1),\\
\mathbb P_M(X=1,Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=0))
&=(1-p)\gamma_A=A(1,1).
\end{aligned}
\]
The two \(X\)-row masses are \(p\) and \(1-p\), including when either is zero.  Hence normalization of \(A\) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P_M(X=0,Y=0\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=0))
&=p-a=A(0,0),\\
\mathbb P_M(X=1,Y=0\mid\operatorname{do}(Z=0))
&=1-p-A(1,1)=A(1,0).
\end{aligned}
\]
Similarly, under \(\operatorname{do}(X=0)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb P_M(Z=0,Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=0))
&=w00t_{00}+w10t_{10}\\
&=n_{00}+n_{10}=c+(b-c)=b=B(0,1),\\
\mathbb P_M(Z=1,Y=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X=0))
&=(1-r)\gamma_B=B(1,1),\\
\mathbb P_M(Z=0,Y=0\mid\operatorname{do}(X=0))
&=r-b=B(0,0),\\
\mathbb P_M(Z=1,Y=0\mid\operatorname{do}(X=0))
&=1-r-B(1,1)=B(1,0).
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the constructed model belongs to \(MC(A,B)\).  Under \(\operatorname{do}(X=0,Z=0)\), its risk is
\[
\begin{aligned}
q
&=\sum_{i,j\in D}w_{ij}t_{ij}\\
&=n_{00}+n_{01}+n_{10}+n_{11}\\
&=c+(a-c)+(b-c)+d=a+b-c+d.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves the lift on every support face.

For the required exact stress test, take
\[
A=((1/8,3/8),(3/8,1/8)),
\qquad
B=((3/8,1/8),(3/8,1/8)).
\]
Then \(p=r=1/2\), \(a=3/8\), \(b=1/8\), all four \(w_{ij}\) equal \(1/4\), and \(cL=cU=1/8\).  Choose \(c=1/8\), use \(d=0\) for the lower model and \(d=1/4\) for the upper model.  The response probabilities are
\[
(t_{00},t_{01},t_{10},t_{11})=(1/2,1,0,0)
\quad\text{or}\quad
(1/2,1,0,1),
\]
and \(\gamma_A=\gamma_B=1/4\).  The distinct thresholds lie in \(\{0,1/4,1/2,1\}\), so in both models one may use an independent \(W0\) with ordered-threshold masses \(1/4,1/4,1/2\).  Directly,
\[
w00t_{00}+w01t_{01}=1/8+1/4=3/8,
\qquad
(1-p)\gamma_A=1/8,
\]
so the four \(A\)-cells, in \((x,y)\)-lexicographic order, are
\[
(1/8,3/8,3/8,1/8).
\]
Likewise,
\[
w00t_{00}+w10t_{10}=1/8,
\qquad
(1-r)\gamma_B=1/8,
\]
so the four \(B\)-cells, in \((z,y)\)-lexicographic order, are
\[
(3/8,1/8,3/8,1/8).
\]
Finally,
\[
q=\frac14(1/2+1+0+t_{11})
\]
equals \(3/8\) and \(5/8\), respectively.  Thus both endpoint SCMs use mutually independent roots, one deterministic outcome assignment per model, and agree exactly with all eight prescribed cells.
added_lemmas.justification: The common ordered-threshold construction lifts every feasible mass pair on the entire closed probability simplex without coupling the two source roots.
added_lemmas.gap: Generic finite canonicalization and polynomial optimization do not themselves provide this explicit at-most-eight-point, source-preserving certificate with null-stratum branches.
added_lemmas.consumer: This theorem supplies the common-SCM attainment step for the closed-simplex compatibility frontier, sharp interval, rational endpoint certificates, and constant-time procedure.

Define \(t_{ij}=n_{ij}/w_{ij}\) when \(w_{ij}>0\), and define \(t_{ij}=0\) when \(w_{ij}=0\).  Define \(\gamma_A=A(1,1)/(1-p)\) when \(1-p>0\), with \(\gamma_A=0\) when \(p=1\); define \(\gamma_B=B(1,1)/(1-r)\) when \(1-r>0\), with \(\gamma_B=0\) when \(r=1\).  Take independent \(D\)-valued roots \(U0,V0\) satisfying \(\Pr(U0=0)=p\) and \(\Pr(V0=0)=r\), and set \(fX(u)=u\), \(fZ(v)=v\).  Put \(h(0,0,u,v)=t_{uv}\), \(h(1,0,u,v)=\gamma_A\), \(h(0,1,u,v)=\gamma_B\), and \(h(1,1,u,v)=1/2\).  Order the distinct values in \(\{t_{00},t_{01},t_{10},t_{11},\gamma_A,\gamma_B,1/2,0,1\}\) as \(0=\lambda_0<\cdots<\lambda_m=1\).  Give the independent private root \(W0\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) mass \(\lambda_k-\lambda_{k-1}\) at \(k\), and set \(fY(x,z,u,v,k)=\mathbf 1\{\lambda_k\le h(x,z,u,v)\}\).  The handle \(Hthr\) returns this finite SCM candidate \(M\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The previous handle described a search and did not specify responses on zero-mass strata or null experimental rows.  The corrected construction gives the ordered-threshold model with explicit zero-denominator branches.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: On input normalized \(2\times2\) probability tables \((A,B)\), compute \((p,r,a,b)\).  Return incompatible exactly when either \(a-b<-(1-p)r\) or \(a-b>p(1-r)\); otherwise return \((qL,qU)\) from their three-branch formulas.  If all cells are rational and the pair is compatible, form the lower endpoint pair \((c,d)=(cU,0)\) and the upper endpoint pair \((c,d)=(cL,w11)\).  For either pair set \(n_{00}=c\), \(n_{01}=a-c\), \(n_{10}=b-c\), and \(n_{11}=d\); use \(t_{ij}=n_{ij}/w_{ij}\) if \(w_{ij}>0\) and \(t_{ij}=0\) if \(w_{ij}=0\).  Use \(\gamma_A=A(1,1)/(1-p)\) if \(1-p>0\) and \(\gamma_A=0\) if \(p=1\); use \(\gamma_B=B(1,1)/(1-r)\) if \(1-r>0\) and \(\gamma_B=0\) if \(r=1\).  Prescribe response probabilities \(t_{uv}\) when \((x,z)=(0,0)\), \(\gamma_A\) when \((x,z)=(1,0)\), \(\gamma_B\) when \((x,z)=(0,1)\), and \(1/2\) when \((x,z)=(1,1)\).  Sort the distinct response probabilities together with \(\{0,1\}\) as \(0=\lambda_0<\cdots<\lambda_m=1\), give \(W0=k\) mass \(\lambda_k-\lambda_{k-1}\), take independent binary \(U0,V0\) with zero-probabilities \(p,r\), set \(fX(u)=u\), \(fZ(v)=v\), and set \(fY(x,z,u,v,k)=\mathbf 1\{\lambda_k\le h(x,z,u,v)\}\) for the prescribed response probability \(h\).  Emit each resulting \(M\in MC(A,B)\) as a lower- or upper-endpoint certificate.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The endpoint generator must avoid dividing by zero on support faces.  Feasibility forces every zero-stratum numerator to vanish, so assigning its unused response probability to zero preserves exact rational certificates.

prose_updates.tldr: For the fixed binary collider with two mutually independent shared roots and private outcome noise, arbitrary normalized experimental tables are compatible exactly when \(-(1-p)r\le a-b\le p(1-r)\), and the all-zero joint-intervention risk has the proved sharp interval \([\max\{a,b,a+b-pr\},\min\{a+1-p,b+1-r,a+b+(1-p)(1-r)\}]\).  One ordered-threshold private root with at most eight support points realizes every interval value while reproducing both complete tables, including all structural-zero faces.  The result yields constant-time endpoints, exact rational endpoint certificates, and a conservative optional sampling interval for this graph and intervention menu.

project_justification.fill: The project derives the two-mass fiber, proves a closed-simplex source-preserving threshold lift with explicit null-stratum branches, and packages the resulting iff test and max/min interval as an exact analytic certificate procedure.  For this fixed input and query the certificate can replace a call to Autobounds' generic polynomial optimizer, while Duarte et al.'s graph-general sharp-optimization theorem remains broader and is not claimed as a new contribution here.

sampling_model.overlap: No positivity or overlap condition is imposed on the population tables: normalization gives \(0\le a\le p\le1\) and \(0\le b\le r\le1\).  On any stratum with zero probability, feasibility forces its target-success numerator to zero and the construction assigns the unused conditional response arbitrarily.

prose_updates.related_work: Gresele et al. formulate structural causal marginal compatibility and explain why overlapping reports must share one response-function law.  Duarte et al., JASA 2024, prove that finite discrete causal bounds with observational or experimental constraints and product disturbance probabilities can be obtained sharply by generic polynomial optimization; their scope permits categorical laws on support faces.  The present result is a closed-simplex analytic specialization for one binary collider, two interventions, and one risk: it derives the compatibility inequality, closed-form endpoints, and small common-SCM certificates rather than strengthening the graph-general solver theorem.  Autobounds is therefore the same-input software consumer whose generic optimization can be replaced by this certificate on the stated specialization.  Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim provide graph-preserving finite canonical SCM representations, but not this eight-point menu-specific lift or formula.  Sachs et al. give symbolic response-function bounds under linear constraints, while the independent latent-source factorization here must be preserved explicitly.  Zaffalon et al., IJAR 2023, provide adjacent multi-source approximate inner bounding through causal EM rather than the exact compatibility and sharp closed-form result proved here.  Shridharan and Iyengar, Finkelstein and Shpitser, and Balke and Pearl provide related optimization, logical-bound, and response-type machinery, but no checked result among them states this fixed collider formula.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The universal source-preserving extension is proved for arbitrary normalized tables, including degenerate treatment marginals and zero-mass natural-treatment strata.  Its product-root assumption remains load-bearing: allowing a root shared by \(X\) and \(Z\), or otherwise correlating \(U0\) and \(V0\), can move the target outside the independent-source interval.  The at-most-eight-point private-root bound is a constructive upper bound, not an optimal-support theorem.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved result concerns only the fixed binary graph \(X\to Y\leftarrow Z\) with the two stated independent shared roots, private outcome noise, the two complete intervention tables, and the risk under \(\operatorname{do}(X=0,Z=0)\).  Structural zeros are included.  A strictly positive-width conclusion is valid only under the additional interior condition \(0<p,r<1\); support faces may point-identify the risk.  Correlated or dependence-budget shared roots, different study populations, a simultaneous region for all four joint-intervention risks, three or more parents, minimal support, tie-optimal inference, a general thicket compiler, and any field-tier claim remain outside scope.  If regime \(B\) is omitted, the mass accounting gives \(q\in[a,a+1-p]\); symmetrically, omitting regime \(A\) gives \(q\in[b,b+1-r]\).
